title: KTÜ students' AI early-warning app pings phones about 30 seconds before a Kulu quake is felt at the Turkish parliament, 15 May 2025
summary: KTÜ students' AI quake app alerted phones about 30 s before a Kulu quake (DHA 5.2, USGS 5.0) was felt at Turkey's parliament, 15 May 2025.
account: On 15 May 2025 software-engineering students from Karadeniz Technical University were presenting their Erken Uyarı Merkezi (Early Warning Center), described in DHA's report as an AI-based earthquake early-warning system, to members of parliament in the TBMM Public Relations building in Ankara when a quake centered in Kulu, Konya, was felt in the capital; DHA gave the magnitude as 5.2, while USGS lists M5.0 at 15:46 local time (12:46:37 UTC), 14 km east-north-east of Kulu at 10 km depth. Student Birkan Yılmaz said notifications had reached their phones 30 seconds before the quake, and students, some MPs and building staff went outside. The fetched reports mention no damage or injuries.
purpose: A student-built earthquake early-warning system meant to notify phones before shaking arrives; warning the room before the Kulu quake was felt was that intended function, demonstrated live during the team's own presentation to MPs.
system: Erken Uyarı Merkezi (Early Warning Center), AI-based earthquake early-warning system built by Karadeniz Technical University software-engineering students
developer: Karadeniz Technical University (KTÜ) software-engineering students (DHA); no company or faculty lead named
deployer: The KTÜ student team, demonstrating the system at the TBMM Public Relations building
domain: Disaster risk reduction / earthquake early warning
taxonomy_note: No category names early warning; Accessibility is the closest, as in the Android-alert records, because the documented effect is that people in the room received a timely alert. Protective response with prevention unproven: the alert preceded the shaking and people left the building, but a quake felt in Ankara from Kulu caused no reported damage, so no counterfactual injury is established.

ratings.reason: MPs, students and staff in the TBMM Public Relations building got about 30 seconds' notice, on the developer's own account, and went outside; no damage or injury is reported, so the benefit is the notice itself.

ai_role.statement: The system is called yapay zeka tabanlı (AI-based) in DHA's report, on the students' description; none of the fetched reports explains how it detects quakes, what data it uses, or whether the alert time was logged. The 30-second lead is the statement of student Birkan Yılmaz, a member of the team that built it, carried by DHA and reproduced by Haberler, Yeni Akit and Yeni Çağ; no MP, AFAD or Kandilli comment on the alert was found. Leaving the building was a human response to the notification and to the shaking.

produced_by: A quake large enough to be felt in Ankara from an epicentre in Kulu, Konya (DHA 5.2; USGS M5.0 at 10 km depth), leaving a gap between detection and the arrival of shaking in the capital
The team's own phones carrying the app, with connectivity inside the TBMM building, during a live demonstration to MPs
An audience already primed by the presentation to treat the notification as a cue to leave
must_hold: The alert must arrive before the shaking; here the lead time is the developer's statement, with no independent log or official timing
The detection source and false-alarm rate are undocumented in the fetched reports, so reliability beyond this one event is unknown
Recipients must act on the notice; here students, some MPs and staff went outside

metric: notifications had reached their phones 30 seconds before the quake

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. All four readable sources carry the same DHA report; ensonhaber.com and gercekgundem.com returned HTTP 403 and were not read. USGS lists the Kulu event as M5.0 mww at 2025-05-15T12:46:37 UTC, 10 km depth, 14 km ENE of Kulu; DHA reports 5.2. The system name Erken Uyarı Merkezi appears in the Yeni Çağ texts. No KTÜ, AFAD or parliamentary statement was found; web search was unavailable in this session. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven as the classifier proposed: the warning is documented only by the developer's statement in a DHA report, and no harm was averted.
